title: At a research centre in Provence
description: Introduce yourself at a research centre, ask simple questions, say where you come from, ask for help and follow directions in French, and find out who does research at Cadarache and ITER.

sources.title: French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives; created 18 October 1945 under Charles de Gaulle; 'énergies alternatives' added to the name in March 2010; slightly over 21,000 staff (21,763 in the CEA's key figures for 2023).

sources.title: CEA: the CEA's centres (cea.fr)
sources.note: Nine centres: Paris-Saclay, Grenoble, Marcoule, Cadarache, DAM Île-de-France, Valduc, Cesta, Le Ripault and Gramat.

sources.title: French National Centre for Scientific Research (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Centre national de la recherche scientifique; founded 19 October 1939; headquarters in Paris; the largest public research body in Europe; about 33,000 staff (2021); fundamental research in all fields.

sources.title: Cadarache (Wikipedia)
sources.note: A CEA centre in the north of Bouches-du-Rhône, near Saint-Paul-lez-Durance; research since 1959; over 5,000 people; energy research (fission reactors and fuel, nuclear waste, fusion, solar). Its ITER schedule (first plasma 2025) is outdated.

sources.title: WEST (formerly Tore Supra) (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Tore Supra operated 1988–2010; WEST first plasma December 2016; a plasma of 1,337 s on 12 February 2025.

sources.title: EUROfusion: World record fusion plasma in Europe (CEA news)
sources.note: WEST at CEA Cadarache held a plasma for 1,337 seconds on 12 February (2025), 25 % longer than the record set in China weeks before.

sources.title: ITER Organization: 20 years ago, the ITER site decision (7 July 2025)
sources.note: On 28 June 2005 in Moscow the ITER Members agreed unanimously to build ITER at Cadarache; the other candidate was Rokkasho in Japan.

sources.title: ITER Organization: ITER France
sources.note: 180-hectare parcel and 42-hectare platform; the CEA Cadarache centre is ITER's host and neighbour; the PACA International School in Manosque began in 2007.

sources.title: ITER Organization: Visiting ITER
sources.note: About 35 km north of Aix-en-Provence; visitors at least 16 years old.

sources.title: ITER (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Seven members; ITER Agreement signed in Paris on 21 November 2006; 2024 baseline: start of research operation 2034, deuterium–tritium operation 2039.

sources.title: ITER Organization: baseline press conference summary (July 2024)
sources.note: The proposed 2024 baseline: start of research operation in 2034, deuterium–tritium operation in 2039.

sources.title: Saint-Paul-lez-Durance (Wikipédia)
sources.note: Commune of Bouches-du-Rhône, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, home of Cadarache and ITER.

sources.title: Storey (Wikipedia): numbering of floors
sources.note: France: the ground floor is the *rez-de-chaussée* and the first floor is one level up; Finland numbers the ground floor as the first.
